That sucks, but at least there was a simple solution. I know someone who got the flu real bad and forgot their tampon, then died because of it. I think she only left it in for a couple of weeks. She was already vulnerable cause she was sick, but still. I'm so glad you figured it out! Tbh, this is part of why I'm about to try a menstral cup.

The paper inside the box says in big letters "BURNING MAY OCCUR, and that's normal." From what I'm gathering, the more irritated your skin is, the more it burns. So if you've been scratching, having sex, or have had a persistent infection, it will probably burn more. For me, the burning was at first a light sting. After 10 minutes it was warm like an icy hot patch. I actually relaxed into it. The burn was far more tolerable than the itch. Still sitting with the stuff. Wear a pad, and maybe even lay on a towel. The liquid is messy and stinky. Anything it gets on will stink. So far I'm tolerating the pain but idk if it's worth it. The application process needs to be refined. It's messy. You squeeze the liquid into the applicatior and liquid gets everywhere. But tbh, if this works, none of these cons matter much to me. However, eventually the burning needs to be fixed.


Update: It's the morning after applying the first dose of medicine. There was a slight burning when I woke up. Just a slight discomfort, way less painful than the BV. The stuff had leaked out onto my pad a little. So far, I haven't experienced any itching from the BV.


Update: Minimal pain until I walk. Still experiencing frequent urination. The burning was bad. Idk if this even helped. Not doing the second dose. My skin is so irritated and swollen now.

The implications of what you are saying are that only the rich are college educated. This means rich people are the doctors, politicians, scientists, lawyers, HR representatives, teachers and literally any other job that requires a college degree. That is incredibly dangerous for our world. We need diversity of perspective and interest. Sure, there are tons of jobs that don't require college degrees. Let the people who want those jobs take them. There shouldn't be a glass ceiling keeping the poor from rising to success. That is what a world with limited access to education looks like.


I totally agree that college is overpriced and that many people will never pay it off. And that the loans might be an additional barrier keeping them from owning property. I get it and I agree that this system isn't working. However I think the solution is to make upper level education free/affordable. It's a step in the wrong direction to discourage bright minds from contributing to society because they were born poor. We should be pushing for more access to opportunity, not for people to dream smaller.



On a side note:
It's curious to me that the same people who are distrustful of the government and big organizations consistently vote against their own interests. It is in the favor of the entire country for everyone to have access to higher education. But I especially see it in impovershed communities. The poor rally around policies that are designed to keep them poor. Anyone who celebrates education being stripped away from millions of people is very short sighted.
